title: Microsoft Entra ID: identity-verified account recovery for users who lose all sign-in methods (Android, iOS, desktop)
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a beta Graph API for the Conditional Access global exclusion that the briefing reports as undocumented. The TAP-free Android guidance also omits the documented requirement to keep TAP issuance on for Android Management API work-profile users.

claims.claim: The feature is Microsoft Entra ID account recovery.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra: ID Account Recovery

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Account recovery restores organisational account access after loss of all registered authentication methods through identity verification.
claims.quote: Account recovery is a Microsoft Entra ID capability that enables users to regain access to their organizational accounts when they lose all registered authentication methods

claims.claim: SSPR requires at least one surviving authentication method, whereas account recovery re-establishes identity trust.
claims.quote: Unlike self-service password reset (SSPR), which requires users to retain at least one authentication method, account recovery re-establishes trust in a user's identity through third-party identity verification before restoring access.

claims.claim: Recovery uses Verified ID and Face Check with third-party identity verification providers.
claims.quote: Uses Microsoft Entra Verified ID and Face Check alongside third-party identity verification providers available through the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: The user identifies their account at sign-in and indicates that they cannot access it.
claims.quote: The user provides their account identifier at sign-in and indicates they can't access their account.

claims.claim: The flow redirects the user to the provider specified in the applicable profile.
claims.quote: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider specified in their applicable profile.

claims.claim: After verification, a Verified ID credential is stored in Microsoft Authenticator.
claims.quote: Upon successful verification, the user receives a verifiable credential (Verified ID) stored in Microsoft Authenticator.

claims.claim: The user presents the new Verified ID to Entra ID for validation.
claims.quote: The user presents their newly acquired Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID. The system validates the credential's authenticity.

claims.claim: Account validation uses directory claim mappings, a custom authentication extension, or both.
claims.quote: Account validation then uses the profile's configured directory claim mappings, a custom authentication extension, or both.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: When recovery is enabled, TAP issuance is on by default.
claims.quote: TAP issuance is on by default for new and existing tenants. This default controls the registration path when recovery is enabled; it doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: The TAP-based flow guides the user to register new authentication methods such as passkeys.
claims.quote: By default, the user receives a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) with limited validity and is guided through registering new authentication methods, such as passkeys.

claims.claim: Learn documents the Account recovery Settings blade as preview.
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Scope; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Account recovery policy is disabled for new and existing tenants until an administrator enables it.
claims.quote: In the new Account recovery policy experience, the policy is disabled by default for both new and existing tenants. Enable the policy before users can use account recovery.

claims.claim: Earlier-preview tenants must also enable the new Account recovery policy.
claims.quote: If your tenant already uses account recovery from an earlier preview, you also need to enable the new policy to continue using the feature.

claims.claim: Creating a profile or setting Production mode does not enable the tenant's recovery policy.
claims.quote: For a recovery profile, Production mode alone doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: The default TAP setting does not enable account recovery, and actions after recovery are separate from tenant enablement.
claims.quote: Enabling the policy is separate from configuring actions after recovery, such as issuing a TAP or removing stale credentials. The default TAP issuance setting doesn't enable account recovery for your tenant.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator manages Account recovery settings.
claims.quote: The Authentication Policy Administrator role to manage Account recovery settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) reaches the policy's settings page.
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview).
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) > Account recovery policy', as the cited page instructs enabling the tenant's Account recovery policy inside Account recovery settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API operation for enabling the tenant's Account recovery policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph account recovery policy enable disable; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph accountRecovery policy; Policy.ReadWrite.Recovery recoveryPolicy. Read recovery setup, overview, Graph create-profile reference and permission excerpts; none gives the tenant-policy enable operation.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) > Actions after recovery reaches the TAP issuance and cleanup settings section.
claims.quote: Use Actions after recovery in Account recovery settings to choose how users register replacement methods.
claims.fix: Give the deciding setting labels in note: 'In Actions after recovery, choose Issue Temporary Access Pass; Stale credential cleanup is available only with TAP issuance off.' Keep the existing section path, which correctly reaches these controls.

claims.claim: Turning TAP issuance off and enabling stale-credential cleanup are preview options.
claims.quote: Turning TAP issuance back on turns cleanup off before saving. Both controls are preview settings.

claims.claim: With attestation required, the TAP-free path is described as supported only on Android without stating the Android work-profile exception.
claims.quote: Android alone doesn't establish eligibility. For users enrolled through Android Management API (AM API), configure recovery to issue a TAP at completion instead of requiring passkey setup.
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'For users enrolled through Android Management API (AM API), keep TAP issuance on and issue a TAP at completion instead of requiring passkey setup.' In the device open question, acknowledge that this AM API exception is already documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/self-service-account-recovery.

claims.claim: With TAP issuance off and cleanup enabled, previously registered methods are deleted after recovery and replacement-passkey registration succeed.
claims.quote: When cleanup is enabled, it deletes all previously registered authentication methods after both recovery and registration of the replacement passkey succeed. The newly registered passkey isn't deleted.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API operation for the recovery TAP-issuance and stale-credential-cleanup settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph account recovery settings TAP isEnabled; account recovery policy Issue Temporary Access Pass stale credential cleanup API. Read recovery setup, overview, FAQ and Graph TAP deletion excerpts; these do not document automation for the recovery settings.

claims.claim: Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles reaches profile management in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Create and manage profiles in Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles.
claims.fix: Keep this documented management-page path and clarify in note: 'For creation, select Create profile, set Profile purpose to Recovery, and choose Evaluation on Profile mode.' The remaining wizard is documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/verified-id/how-to-create-id-verification-profile.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles creates an ID verification profile with configuration in the request body.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles

claims.claim: verifiedIdUsageConfigurations defines profile purpose including recovery, onboarding or all.
claims.quote: verifiedIdUsageConfigurations | verifiedIdUsageConfiguration collection | Collection defining the usage purpose for the profile. The possible values are: recovery, onboarding, all, unknownFutureValue. Required.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least-privileged role for the profile-creation API.
claims.quote: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview) > Global exclusions > Account onboarding and recovery (Preview) reaches the global exclusion.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview). Under Global exclusions, enable the Account onboarding and recovery (Preview) exclusion.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the Conditional Access global onboarding and recovery exclusion.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings
"exclusions": { "allResourcesExclusions": { "userActionExclusions": [ { "state": "enabled", "userAction": "accountrecovery" } ] } }
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to kind graph, call 'PATCH /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/conditionalaccesssettings-update?view=graph-rest-beta'. Add to note: 'Beta API: exclusions.allResourcesExclusions.userActionExclusions sets the exclusion through userAction accountrecovery and state enabled or disabled; supply the complete desired collection. Beta APIs are not supported for production applications.' Replace the prose absence with 'Microsoft Graph documents the global exclusion through the beta Conditional Access settings API; APIs for the recovery policy and actions after recovery are not yet documented.' Add that API source.

claims.where: controls[3]: governs and note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The global exclusion affects every Conditional Access policy targeting All resources and covers account recovery.
claims.quote: This setting affects all policies targeting All resources, not just the policy used in your pilot.

claims.claim: Policies directly targeting the Account onboarding and recovery user action still apply when the global exclusion is enabled.
claims.quote: Enabling the exclusion removes the Account onboarding and recovery user action from All resources policies; policies that directly target the user action still apply.

claims.claim: Conditional Access protection for the Account onboarding and recovery user action is configured separately from the profile.
claims.quote: A shared profile and a Conditional Access policy are separate configuration tasks. Configure policies targeting the Account onboarding and recovery user action separately from the profile.

claims.claim: Identity verification processes government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.
claims.quote: Identity verification involves processing government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Providers have their own privacy and retention terms in their Microsoft Security Store offers.
claims.quote: Identity verification providers have their own privacy and data retention policies as part of the verification offer from the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: Custom authentication extensions are optional for account validation.
claims.quote: Custom authentication extensions — Optional Azure Function, Logic App, or REST API endpoints that add organization-specific account validation logic during recovery.

claims.claim: Data processed by the custom extension stays inside the organisation's trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data processed by the custom authentication extension stays within the organization's trust boundary.

claims.claim: Only the custom extension's match result is returned to the recovery flow.
claims.quote: No organizational data is shared with Microsoft — only the match result is returned to the account recovery flow.

claims.claim: Learn warns that name-only matching may provide insufficient assurance for high-risk accounts.
claims.quote: Name-only matching may not provide sufficient assurance for high-risk accounts.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests a custom extension for additional validation of sensitive populations.
claims.quote: For sensitive user populations, consider enabling a custom authentication extension to validate additional claims beyond first and last name.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Terms of use, Require authentication strength and most other Entra-specific controls are unsupported for recovery and may block it or leave requirements unenforced.
claims.quote: Terms of use, Require authentication strength, and most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls aren't supported for the onboarding and recovery user action. Unsupported recovery policy requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.

claims.quote: For certain accounts — such as those belonging to a CEO or finance controller — you might restrict recovery to in-person or remote processes that include a human in the loop.

claims.claim: Creating a profile in the portal turns on Verified ID as an authentication method for all users.
